d: Delhi is on the brink of a severe air pollution crisis just days before Diwali. The national capital's AQI climbed to 391, with 30 monitoring stations recording severe air quality. Meanwhile, Punjab has reported 2,787 stubble-burning incidents, and Barnala's AQI has reportedly soared to 1,104. As Delhi and Punjab trade blame, the Supreme Court has questioned the role of farm fires, private vehicles, commercialised festivals and urban emissions. With PM2.5 pollution rising and severe air quality forecast through November 8, is North India heading for another public-health emergency? We…
